A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiMuon research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching content across section renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original optimizer experiments on Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and ViT, including perplexity, accuracy, memory, runtime, and learning curves in Tables 2–5 and Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including the ViT learning curves in Appendix C. Results retained from v3 still qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same full-rank and compressed STORM-like updates, randomized SVD, and Newton–Schulz procedures. Added wording about orthogonalization and corrected punctuation do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Mamba-130M on WikiText-103, Qwen2.5-0.5B on MiniPile, and ViT on Tiny-ImageNet. The new 'pre-training' terminology describes experiments already explicitly conducted from scratch in v3.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same evaluated comparators: Adam, AdamW, Lion, SUMO, Muon, and Muon++. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Training budgets remain 5,000, 2,000, and 10,000 iterations for Mamba, Qwen, and ViT, respectively. Batch sizes, preprocessing, rank settings, ten Newton–Schulz steps, metrics, and the ViT target loss of 3.70 are unchanged. PPL abbreviations and directional arrows only relabel existing metrics.

E4.justification: The full-rank versus ranks 4, 8, and 16 comparisons, ViT runtime analysis, and learning curves are retained. Appendix C adds no new ablation, sensitivity test, robustness analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same point estimates and learning curves without reporting empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain all numerical results, and Figures 2–4 retain identical plotted content. For example, full-rank LiMuon validation perplexities remain 47.78 and 40.83, ViT validation Top-1 accuracy remains 48.04%, and time to target remains 7 minutes 1 second. Revised superlatives describe rankings already established in v3.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces v3's 'without loss of generalization' assertion for the polar-error restriction ε_q ∈ (0,1) with an appeal to Theorem 2 of Kim & Oh (2026). This revises the stated mathematical justification; the restriction, convergence bounds, and Appendix A–B proofs remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not independently establish the cited theorem's applicability.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: variance-reduced Muon with reduced memory, improved sample-complexity guarantees, Newton–Schulz analysis, and empirical effectiveness. 'Pre-training' and 'STORM-like' clarify descriptions already supported by v3.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning memory–performance tradeoffs, training stability, and applicability to state-space, language, and vision models are retained. No substantive mechanism explanation, applicability boundary, failure condition, or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix C's hyperparameters and search ranges are identical, as are the hardware, architecture, preprocessing, and training-setting disclosures. There is no change to code or data access information.

R1.justification: The bibliography and novelty positioning remain unchanged, but Section 4.2 newly identifies Theorem 2 of the already cited Kim & Oh (2026) as support for the polar-error restriction. This is a limited refinement of the stated dependence on prior work.

P1.justification: The experiment hierarchy is corrected from Sections 6, 7, and 7.1 to subsections 5.1–5.3. v5 also standardizes smoothness terminology, labels the existing studies as pre-training, and makes localized prose and appendix-heading edits without substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Tables 2–4 gain metric-direction arrows and revised headings; Tables 2–3 use PPL abbreviations and adjusted spacing. Table 5 newly emphasizes the best time-to-target value. Figures retain their content with minor placement or scaling adjustments, and Appendix C's displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects the experimental section hierarchy, improves table readability, and makes the attribution supporting the polar-error condition more explicit. These provide modest gains in organization and traceability while preserving the scientific content and complete appendices. The revision does not demonstrate stronger empirical evidence or independently resolve the theoretical condition's justification.
